stem.en: Suppose the wall of a plant cell became as flexible as a cell membrane. What would you expect if this cell were placed in a concentrated sugar solution?

text.en: It would lose water and the whole cell would shrink.
It would stop losing water, because a flexible wall can hold water more tightly than a rigid one.

feedback.en: Osmosis still takes water out of the cell. A flexible wall would not stop this.

text.en: Its outer outline would stay the same size and only its inner content would become smaller.

feedback.en: That is what a rigid wall makes possible. A flexible wall would shrink with the cell.

text.en: It would gain water from the solution and become much firmer than an ordinary plant cell.

feedback.en: Water leaves a cell for a more concentrated solution, so the cell would not gain water.

explanation.en: A flexible wall could not hold the outline, so the cell would behave like a cheek cell in sugar. A plant made of such cells could not stay firm or upright either.

hints.en: Which cell has no rigid layer, and what did it do in sugar?
